content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, I notice some clear patterns:

**Example 1 (2024-11-28):**
- History is around 68.47
- Model forecasts start at 68.18 (slightly below current)
- But true outcomes quickly move higher, ending around 76.92
- The model seems to be under-predicting significantly

**Example 2 (2024-12-27):**
- History is around 69.47
- Model forecasts: start at 70.93, 70.90, 71.48...
- True outcomes: 71.56, 71.98, 73.00, 75.19, 75.94, 76.92...
- Model is UNDER-predicting by significant margins

**Example 3 (2024-11-27):**
- Very similar to Example 1, just 1 day earlier
- Model forecasts start at 68.92 vs true 68.47 (slightly higher, but then falls behind)
- By day 10+, model is ~2-3 points below reality
- True outcomes are consistently higher than forecasts

**Example 4 (2024-11-29):**
- Almost identical to Example 1 (just shifted 2 days)
- Same pattern: model forecasts are too low
- By day 10, model is ~2-4 points below reality
- By day 20+, the gap widens to 5-7 points

**Example 5 (2024-12-19):**
- Uses data from Example 2 but at a different date
- Model forecasts start at 67.48 vs history of 69.86
- But then model forecasts 67.67, 68.68, 68.03, 69.49, 70.08, 71.79, 71.85, 69.74, 68.72, 66.11, 66.50, 67.12, 68.08, 67.52, 67.58, 67.34, 67.80, 68.27, 68.68, 67.94, 69.75, 70.78, 69.37, 70.70, 73.61, 74.48, 76.47
